learning_outcomes.text: Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated by formulating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Choose and apply the most appropriate methods and techniques to analyze and solve problems defined by data that represent a challenge due to their volume, velocity, variety, or heterogeneity, including computational, mathematical, statistical, and signal processing methods.

Have the experimental and analytical skills to work autonomously, being able to propose experiments and to describe, analyze, evaluate, and interpret the resulting information to propose alternative and novel solutions to known and/or emerging problems.
Create models and make decisions based on available data, combining acquired knowledge and being able to apply new knowledge to solve problems.
Ability to integrate into a multidisciplinary team within the framework of a data science project.
Ability to express data processing results clearly and convincingly, both in writing and orally.
Know the fundamentals of programming and basic algorithmic techniques and apply them using the most relevant programming languages in the field of data science and engineering.
Evaluate the computational complexity of a problem and identify, if they exist, appropriate algorithmic strategies for its resolution.
Know the object-oriented programming paradigm (inheritance, polymorphism, exceptions).
Know linear and non-linear data structures.
Manage class libraries for the representation of object containers (sets, files, etc.).
Know and manage the basic concepts of multi-threading programming.

syllabus_topics: Object-Oriented Programming: Inheritance (single and multiple, visibility of data and methods) and Polymorphism (dynamic binding, method overriding).
Data Structures: Linear structures (lists, stacks, and queues) and non-linear structures (graphs and trees). Traversal and search algorithms. Other structures (sets, dictionaries, hash tables, etc.).

assessment_methods.method: Attendance / Participation in Seminars and Tutorials (includes online)
Active Participation in Forums and Virtual Campus Activities

assessment_rules: To pass the course in the ordinary examination, it is necessary to obtain a grade equal to or greater than 4.5 out of 10 in both the theoretical final exam and the total practical part. Any grade lower than 4.5 in either of these two parts will result in failing the course. If a student does not participate in enough evaluation activities to reach at least 50% of the weight, they will be considered "No Presentado". For extraordinary examinations, the theoretical final exam accounts for 60% and the practical final exam for 40%. In extraordinary examinations, a minimum of 4.5 out of 10 is required in both exams to pass.
